structs.name: CharacterModifyResponseRecord

fields.name: header
fields.notes: Reserved/unknown header bytes. Not read by FUN_00DA79D0; may carry sequence or framing that the outer dispatcher (BCS-Y-0018) consumes.

fields.name: validity_flag
fields.notes: FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024) skips processing if this byte is 0.

fields.name: command
fields.notes: CharacterModify sub-command. Values observed: 1 = RESERVE, 2 = MAKE, 3 = RENAME, 4 = DELETE, 6 = RENAME_RETAINER. The c2s request uses the same values at a different offset and width (u8 at 0x11).

fields.name: unknown_0C
fields.notes: Not read by the decoded handlers; reserved.

fields.name: player_id
fields.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[pid]'. Used as the join key for CMD_RENAME's list walk: each existing slot entry whose first dword equals this gets the new name + doRename flag patched in place.

fields.name: character_id
fields.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[cid]'.

fields.name: slot_or_chrindex
fields.notes: Character slot index, read as a single byte by FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024): `*(byte *)(body + 0x18)` on the CMD_MAKE path, bounds-checked against the local slot count and then passed to the 0x2E0-stride slot indexer FUN_006B3D40 (BCS-Y-0096). Logged through the byte-value numeric ostream overload FUN_005434A0 (BCS-Y-1823), not the const char* overload, so the u8 width is parser-confirmed. The server and the parity baseline both write a u32 type constant 0x400017 across body+0x18..0x1B; little-endian that puts 0x17 (23) in the byte this parser reads, which exceeds any real slot count, so CMD_MAKE always takes the 'INVALID CHRINDEX 23 for MAKECHR' log branch and falls through to the append path rather than the in-place REPLACE path. That is the correct outcome for a newly created character, which is why the live client accepts the packet. The remaining three bytes of the server's constant are unread by this parser (see unknown_1A).

fields.name: do_rename
fields.notes: Per-entry needs-rename flag. CMD_RENAME copies this byte into the existing matched character entry at entry+9.

fields.name: unknown_1A
fields.notes: Not read by the decoded handlers.

fields.name: ticket
fields.notes: Logged as 'MAKECHR[tkt]'.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Character name. Logged as 'MAKECHR[nam]'. Copied into the existing matched character entry at entry+4 on CMD_RENAME.

fields.name: world_name
fields.notes: World name, NUL-terminated ASCII. FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024) logs it as 'MAKECHR[wld]' by passing the ADDRESS body+0x40 to the const char* ostream overload FUN_004E7290 (BCS-Y-1821), in the identical two-call shape it uses for the character name at body+0x20; the pid / cid / ticket fields at body+0x10 / +0x14 / +0x1C instead load their value and pass it to the numeric overload FUN_00DA9670 (BCS-Y-1822). The overload split is the parser-side proof that body+0x40 is a string, not a scalar. Supersedes the earlier `world_id` uint32_t reading, which was a decode error, not a server error: the server writes a 32-byte padded ASCII world name here (kLobbyCharaCreatorWorldNameSize = 0x20), matching the parity baseline, and the live 1.23b client accepts it. Width 0x20 is taken from the server / parity-baseline field size; the parser itself only requires NUL termination.

fields.name: remainder
fields.notes: Remaining 368 bytes of the response body. The handler does not read fields past body+0x40 by name; instead bytes from body+0x10 through at least body+0x1E0 are copied into a local 0x2E0-byte buffer (with the trailing 0x110 bytes zeroed) and pushed onto a slot vector via FUN_00891F00. The handler thus implicitly assumes the body extends at least to body+0x1E0 (480 bytes), 16 bytes past the explicitly-named region; see BCS-S-0009 SlotEntry for the slot's interpretation and MDI-014 for the open width question.

structs.notes: s2c body for lobby opcode 0x0E (CharacterModify response). The handler (FUN_00DA79D0 / BCS-Y-0024) explicitly reads fields out to body+0x60 (world_name), but the body must extend to at least body+0x1E0 (480 bytes) because the push path copies 0x1D0 bytes starting at body+0x10. Documented size 0x1D0 reflects the named-field region; the actual on-the-wire body size remains open and is annotated on the remainder field. Re-anchored against the client parser (see phase-ledger the lobby-0x0e-0x0d-parser-re-anchor pass): the named region now agrees field-for-field with the server / parity-baseline layout (u64 sequence, u8 1, u8 1, u16 command @0x0A, u32 0, u32 pid @0x10, u32 cid @0x14, u32 type constant 0x400017 @0x18, u32 ticket @0x1C, 0x20-byte ASCII name @0x20, 0x20-byte ASCII world name @0x40). Two prior divergences resolved: body+0x40 was catalogued as a u32 `world_id` and is in fact an ASCII string (the parser hands its address to the const char* ostream overload); body+0x18 is genuinely read as a u8 by the client even though the server writes a u32 there, and the resulting 'INVALID CHRINDEX 23' branch is the normal append path for a new character. Shares the chara-list per-character record (BCS-S-0008) stride and feeds the same slot-entry vector (this+0x1D4..this+0x1D8, element stride 0x2E0) via the push path FUN_00891F00 (BCS-Y-0023 = std::vector::push_back). The two layouts are the SAME field frame offset by 0x10: this body's name at body+0x20 lands at slot entry+0x10, which is exactly where BCS-S-0008's record+0x20 name lands (see BCS-S-0008 notes for the three-way frame proof). The push does not source the body directly: the handler builds a local 0x2E0-byte buffer (body+0x10..body+0x1E0 copied to local[0..0x1D0), local[0x1D0..0x2D0) zeroed) and pushes that local. See BCS-S-0009 for the resulting slot layout. Earlier notes incorrectly described FUN_00891F00 as a 're-parser' (it is push_back) and as receiving body directly (it receives the local buffer). The packet is shared across the five sub-commands: the server emits this response after RESERVE/MAKE/RENAME/DELETE/RENAME_RETAINER to deliver the post-operation character state. Distinct from BCS-S-0007 CharacterModifyRequest which the client sends on the c2s side: same opcode, different layout, different command field offset and width (see MDI-024).

structs.name: CharaListPerCharacterRecord

fields.name: header_unknown
fields.notes: Not read by FUN_00DA76B0 per-record loop. For record 0 these bytes are also at body+0..7 (since records are tightly packed starting at body+0). The chara-list outer init-path flag at record+8 and record count at record+9 are read off RECORD 0 only; other records' bytes at the same offsets are unused by the parser.

fields.name: init_flags
fields.notes: Record 0 only: low bits of this byte (masked & 0xFE) control the first-call init path in FUN_00DA76B0 (BCS-Y-0019). 0 means initialize the slot vector from this+0x1D0 before processing records.

fields.name: record_count
fields.notes: Record 0 only: total number of per-character records in this packet. FUN_00DA76B0 loops local_306 from 0 while local_306 < this byte, so the client reads a single byte. The server and the parity baseline write a u32 count at this offset; the two readings are wire-identical for counts below 256 and the client caps the list at 8 entries, so this is a width annotation rather than a contradiction. The u8 width is what the parser actually consumes.

fields.name: header_remainder
fields.notes: Not read by the per-record loop.

fields.name: slot_key
fields.notes: Slot key, low 6 bits (masked with 0x3F). FUN_00DA76B0 walks the existing slot vector at this+0x1D4..this+0x1D8 (entries at stride 0x2E0) looking for an entry whose entry+8 byte matches this value.

fields.name: options_and_pad
fields.notes: record+0x19 is the per-character options byte (doRename bit 0x02, isLegacy bit 0x08 in the server / parity-baseline builder). Not read by the 0x0D parser, but confirmed positionally by the 0x0E handler FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024), whose CMD_RENAME path writes its own do_rename byte into the matched slot entry at entry+0x09 - and slot entry byte X is record byte 0x10+X, so entry+0x09 is record+0x19. Bytes 0x1A..0x1F are the u16 zero pad and the u32 current zone id in the server frame; neither is read by this parser.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Character name, fixed 0x20 bytes of padded ASCII. Not read by the 0x0D parser itself (which bulk-copies record+0x10 onward into the slot entry), but pinned here by the 0x0E handler FUN_00DA79D0 (BCS-Y-0024): its CMD_RENAME path copies 8 dwords (0x20 bytes) from CharacterModify body+0x20 into the matched slot entry at entry+0x10 (`piVar12 = piVar4 + 4` on an int*). Because the 0x0D parser fills a slot entry by copying 0x1D0 bytes starting at record+0x10, slot entry+0x10 IS record+0x20. Supersedes the earlier reading that placed the name at record+0x50: that offset holds a concatenable tail string (see appearance_tail_string), which a fixed-width name could never be. Agrees with the server / parity-baseline entry+0x10 name once the 0x10 frame shift is applied.

fields.name: world_name_and_length_prefix
fields.notes: Not read by FUN_00DA76B0. In the server / parity-baseline entry frame (entry = record+0x10) this span is the 0x0E-byte padded ASCII world name at entry+0x30 (record+0x40..0x4D) followed by the 7-bit-encoded length prefix of the appearance blob at entry+0x3E (record+0x4E). A two-byte prefix there is what puts the blob itself at record+0x50, where the parser does read it. Offsets inside this span are frame-aligned from the server builder, not parser-read.

fields.name: appearance_tail_string
fields.notes: NUL-terminated tail string, variable length within the record bounds. On a slot key match, FUN_00DA76B0 (BCS-Y-0019) strlens this string (length includes the terminator), finds the end of the existing slot entry's string starting at entry+0x40, and APPENDS these bytes there. Slot entry byte X is record byte 0x10+X, so entry+0x40 is record+0x50: the parser is concatenating this same logical field across successive records that share a slot key, which is how a blob longer than one record is paged in. That concatenation is the reason this cannot be the character name - a fixed 0x20-byte name would never be appended to itself. In the server / parity-baseline entry frame this is the length-prefixed appearance data written at entry+0x3E. Supersedes the earlier `name` reading of this offset; the real name is at record+0x20.

fields.name: payload_b
fields.notes: Remaining bytes after the tail string up to record+0x1CF. Sub-field widths not yet decoded.

structs.notes: Per-character record carried by the chara-list lobby packet (opcode 0x0D, dispatched via BCS-Y-0019 FUN_00DA76B0). Walked at stride 0x1D0 starting at body+0 for up to body[9] records (`local_304[0] = param_2 + local_306 * 0x1d0`); record 0's leading 16 bytes double as the outer chara-list header (init flag at +8, record count at +9). Re-anchored against the client parser in phase-ledger the lobby-0x0e-0x0d-parser-re-anchor pass. Frame relationship to the server / parity-baseline builder: the server writes a 0x10-byte list header (u64 sequence, u8 tracker @0x08, u32 count @0x09, u8 0, u16 0) and then entries at body+0x10 + i*0x1D0, so SERVER ENTRY i = CLIENT RECORD i + 0x10. The client's record window is deliberately shifted 0x10 earlier, which is exactly why its copy path sources record+0x10 for 0x1D0 bytes - that source span IS the server's entry. Three independent parser reads confirm the shift: the slot key the client masks at record+0x18 is the server's slot byte at entry+0x08; the do_rename byte the 0x0E handler writes to slot entry+0x09 is the server's options byte at entry+0x09 = record+0x19; and the 0x20-byte name the 0x0E handler writes to slot entry+0x10 is the server's name at entry+0x10 = record+0x20. The prior catalog reading placed the name at record+0x50 - that offset is really the length-prefixed appearance blob, which the parser treats as a NUL-terminated string and CONCATENATES onto the matched slot entry's existing string at entry+0x40, a paging mechanism no fixed-width name could use. The count field is read as a u8 by the client and written as a u32 by the server; the two are wire-identical below 256 and the client caps the list at 8 entries. The push path reads 0x1D0 bytes starting at record+0x10, copies that into a local 0x2E0-byte buffer with the trailing 0x110 bytes zeroed, and pushes onto the slot-entry vector (element size 0x2E0) via FUN_00891F00 (BCS-Y-0023 push_back) when no existing entry matches the record's slot key. The slot-copy-construct path FUN_00891900 has been decoded (chain FUN_00891900 -> FUN_008916F0 -> FUN_008913E0 -> FUN_00891360 / BCS-Y-0076..0079) and reveals the slot's 0x2E0 anatomy (see BCS-S-0009). Sub-field widths inside record+0x60..0x1CF remain undecoded and are still blocked on a payload-shape correlation; no lobby pcap exists, the capture corpus excludes login.

structs.name: CharaMakeSlotEntry

fields.name: wire_mirror
fields.notes: Plain copy of the wire body bytes [+0x10..+0x1E0). For chara-list per-character records (BCS-S-0008), the source is record+0x10..0x1E0. For CharacterModify response bodies (BCS-S-0006), the source is body+0x10..0x1E0. The two source layouts disagree on field positions inside this region: chara-list places the slot key at record+0x18 (low 6 bits) and a variable-length name at record+0x50, which map to slot+0x08 and slot+0x40 respectively; response places slot_or_chrindex at body+0x18 (mapping to slot+0x08) and the 32-byte character name at body+0x20 (mapping to slot+0x10). The parser only relies on slot+0x08 being the slot key in both cases; downstream readers must know which source populated the entry to interpret fields past +0x10.

fields.name: slot_key
fields.notes: Slot key inside wire_mirror, used by the chara-list parser (FUN_00DA76B0 / BCS-Y-0019) for entry lookup. Comparison uses the low 6 bits (masked 0x3F) against the wire record's record+0x18 low 6 bits.

fields.name: response_name_window
fields.notes: 32-byte name region populated only when the slot was filled or patched by the CharacterModify response handler (CMD_RENAME copies the name from body+0x20 here; the push path for the same body would also land it here via wire_mirror). Distinct from chara_list_name_window below.

fields.name: chara_list_name_window
fields.notes: Variable-length name region populated when the slot was filled by the chara-list parser from record+0x50. The chara-list parser scans from slot+0x3F forward to find the tail-string null terminator, then appends additional name bytes from incoming records that match this slot's key.

fields.name: zeroed_local_state
fields.notes: Zeroed at push time by both source paths (chara-list parser and CharacterModify response handler). Use unknown; probably holds slot-local UI state populated after push.

fields.name: embedded_vector
fields.notes: Embedded std::vector with element stride 0x30 = 48 bytes (matching BCS-S-0004 RetainerListRecord exactly). Initialized empty at push time via FUN_00890EE0 (BCS-Y-0080), which copy-constructs from the source local buffer's matching offset (which is also zeroed at push time). Element type confirmed as BCS-S-0004 RetainerListRecord: the upsert helper FUN_00DA94C0 (BCS-Y-0094) operates generically on any container's embedded vector at this+0x2D0, and one of its three callers is FUN_00DA4D80 (BCS-Y-0022 RetainerListParser, opcode 0x17), forcing the records carried in vectors of this exact shape to be BCS-S-0004. The upsert key is the byte at element+8 = low byte of BCS-S-0004's `total` field (a stable per-retainer index). The slot's specific vector is initialized empty by the copy-construct path; all three known FUN_00DA94C0 callsites have been traced to set `this` = CharaMakeSlotEntry, so the populated retainer vector is slot+0x2D0 in every observed path: (1) RetainerListParser FUN_00DA4D80 walks the chara-list slot vector at CharaMakeOperation+0x1D4 by character_id and upserts into each matching slot; (2) CMD_MAKE in FUN_00DA79D0 looks up chara-list-slot[body[0x18]] via the indexer FUN_006B3D40 (BCS-Y-0096) and upserts the installed record; (3) FUN_00DA9550 (BCS-Y-0091) inherits its `this` from FUN_00DA76B0's newly-pushed slot at slot[size-1]. Layout per std::vector implementation: vec+0x00 unused/allocator, vec+0x04 begin pointer, vec+0x08 end pointer, vec+0x0C cap_end pointer.

structs.notes: Slot entry stored in the CharaMakeOperation's slot-entry vectors at this+0x1D4..0x1D8 (chara-list vector, populated by FUN_00DA76B0) and this+0x218..0x21C (response vector, populated by FUN_00DA79D0). Both vectors share the 0x2E0 stride. Decoded from Ghidra 12.1 auto-decompiler analysis of the copy-construct chain FUN_00891900 -> FUN_008916F0 -> FUN_008913E0 -> FUN_00891360 / FUN_00890EE0 at VAs 0x00891900, 0x008916F0, 0x008913E0, 0x00891360, 0x00890EE0. Field widths inside wire_mirror remain blocked on pcap correlation of the chara-list (opcode 0x0D) or CharacterModify response (opcode 0x0E) payloads.
